about.title: Colusa Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Colusa is a small, close-knit river town, and most people here know the shops along Market Street and Fremont Street well enough to notice when something's off — a cracked sidewalk near Bridge Street, a spill left too long in an aisle, poor lighting in a parking area. When a property owner fails to address a hazard they knew about, or should have caught with reasonable upkeep, the person who gets hurt often ends up facing medical bills and missed work with no clear path forward. We handle premises liability claims and can review what happened at the time of your injury. Whether the fall happened at a local business, an apartment complex, or a public building, getting the right documentation early — photos, witness names, incident reports — can matter a great deal. Our team can look at what happened and explain your options, without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Colusa Property Injury

items.title: Notice Is Everything in These Claims
items.desc: California law generally requires showing the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. We can help identify what evidence supports that notice before it disappears.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Doesn't Last Long
items.desc: Many Colusa businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks, so preserving it quickly can be critical to a claim. We can move fast to request that footage be retained before it's gone.

items.title: Your Own Actions Can Still Count Against You — But Not Entirely
items.desc: California applies pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help present your side clearly instead of letting an insurer assign blame unfairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Colusa?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, that deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim to be filed. We can confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: Do most falls happen at a specific time or place in Colusa?
items.answer: Public crash data isn't the same as fall data, but Colusa's reported collision activity does tend to peak on Fridays around midday along corridors like Rt 20, Fremont Street, Bridge Street, and Market Street — a reminder that busy periods can also mean busier, less-maintained property conditions. If your fall happened near one of these areas, mentioning the time and location helps us evaluate foot traffic and maintenance schedules.

items.question: What if I'm not sure the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: That's a common concern, and it's exactly what we investigate — through maintenance logs, prior complaints, inspection records, or how long the hazard was visibly present. You don't need to have all the answers before reaching out; documenting what you saw and any witnesses is a strong starting point.
